descriptionChirho: To draw out or unsheathe a sword or weapon from its sheath, the primary and most frequent sense of שָׁלַף, used of warriors drawing swords in battle contexts (e.g., Judg 8:10, 20:2, 1 Chr 21:5).

labelChirho: pull out, extract from a body
descriptionChirho: To pull out or extract something embedded in a fixed position, such as a weapon drawn from a wound or a stake pulled from the ground (Job 20:25), distinct from unsheathing because the object is lodged rather than stored.

To draw off or remove a sandal as a legal-symbolic act confirming a transaction or renunciation of right, attested in the Ruth 4:7-8 custom of חֲלִיצָה where one party removes his shoe and gives it to the other.
